critical_code_review_comments: routes/attendance_core.py is 3,576 lines — largest single route module in the codebase. Consider splitting into sub-modules on the next refactor pass: (a) employee punch flow (punch/today/history/my-month) ~1,200 lines; (b) admin ops (roster/manual-punch/approve/audit) ~1,400 lines; (c) payroll compute engine (_compute_payroll_run + helpers) ~700 lines. Same file-size concern flagged for employees_admin.py in Iter 397.

server.py still 14,424 lines. The bottom re-export block for shared helpers (_parse_any_date, _month_is_after_exit, _month_is_before_doj, _month_is_complete, _payslip_is_processed, _onboarding_payroll_exclusion, apply_contractual_gate, MessageCreate, punch) is fragile — any additional module that imports 'from server import X' at import-time will circular-fault if X isn't re-exported. Consider moving these helpers to a dedicated /app/backend/shared/ package so no module ever needs to import from server.

/api/admin/attendance/roster/mark ignores any payload-supplied date and hard-codes today (line 1957 of attendance_core.py: `today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')`). If the intent is 'mark today's roster only' that's fine, but the endpoint name doesn't suggest that restriction. Consider either accepting an optional `date` on RosterMarkRequest or renaming to /roster/mark-today.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_iter398_attendance_core_refactor.py for future regression on the attendance core cluster. Key gotchas encoded in the tests: (1) /admin/attendance/manual-punch schema is {user_id, kind, at, reason} (NOT date/in_time/out_time); (2) DELETE /admin/attendance/{record_id} requires ?reason=... QUERY param (not body); (3) /admin/attendance/roster/mark schema is {marks:[{user_id, action}], note?} and action must be 'in'|'out'|'absent' (NOT status/weekoff); the endpoint hard-codes TODAY. (4) /admin/attendance/day-status/{cid} needs BOTH from_date & to_date query params or returns 422. (5) Employee login for TEST50 is via {login_id:'TEST50', pin:'123456'} to /auth/pin-login. openapi is only reachable via http://localhost:8001/openapi.json (not through the public ingress).
